interpretation: Fresh native devices with the same CPU frustum set. Both controls add one equal-size queue write per camera list; only ascending versus fixed-seed shuffled instance order changes within each experiment. Actual GPU storage indices must match the intervention, and their sorted set must be identical. Reflection lists, source matrices/materials, camera and physical state are unchanged. flatPayload selects a diagnostic-only color/seed vertex payload candidate; continuousShadow selects smooth world-space PCF rotation instead of a discontinuous half-metre hash. lightingProbe observes selected fragment values in the normal attachment while preserving production color arithmetic; subsequent effects use probe values instead of normals, and captured images are not render quality evidence. The velocity-input probe duplicates interpolated in.velocity in another binary16 MRT; velocityExportChecks compares every geometry-covered x/y word exactly, excluding and counting depth-clear background. An opaqueBoundary probe also compares these duplicate exports at pass end. Shader instrumentation may change compiler scheduling. Candidate module hashes and probe channel meanings are recorded. Every captured stage channel is compared exactly against ascending references; shadowInputs additionally reads the initial static map, per-frame dynamic shadow, Frame uniform and light source/cell buffers. instanceInputs reads every camera batch source buffer, requires exact equality with production CPU 40-float records and compares repeat hashes. readbackChecks compares native opaque/normal binary16 copies with independent compute textureLoad binary32 bitcasts and another native copy without a new render. For velocity-input it also checks packed RG16 velocity against the independent binary32 path and a repeated packed read; the packed specular codec is not independently validated. opaqueBoundary captures all four MRT outputs immediately after the opaque pass in the original command encoder and compares them with the same textures after the full frame; the fixture must have no transparent or snow draws. Observations preserve original texture usage but can alter GPU scheduling; render shaders are unchanged only when shader intervention flags are absent. Missing checks fail coverage; disagreements fail their agreement gates and strict repeatability. Same-order repeat SHA256 is checked independently. Additional dispatches/readbacks/waits are correctness observations, not performance measurements. Divergence and same-order repeatability must be considered together: variation alone does not establish deterministic dependence on instance order or identify a shader/driver cause.
